FISA created a court process for foreign intelligence surveillance inside the United States. After September 11 Congress widened collection, then in 2008 added Section 702 for targeting foreigners abroad through U.S. providers, then in 2015 ended bulk telephone records collection. The live questions concern sunsets and how agencies may search lawfully collected data for Americans' information.

## What you should be able to do

- Explain what the FISA court must find before approving traditional surveillance.
- Describe how Section 702 differs from an individual FISA order.
- Track the sunset and reauthorization history of Section 702.

[FISA](../../statutes/fisa-1978.qmd) [1978]{.reading-year} [Partly expired]{.status .status-partly-expired} [Framework statute]{.layer-badge}

Created a judicial process for foreign intelligence surveillance inside the United States.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/92/1783), [current code](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/50/1801?link-type=html)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="fisa-1978"> I have read this</label>

::: {.reading-card .domain-intelligence data-statute="patriot-2001"}
[USA PATRIOT Act](../../statutes/patriot-2001.qmd) [2001]{.reading-year} [Partly expired]{.status .status-partly-expired} [Specific authorization]{.layer-badge}

An omnibus counterterrorism law passed six weeks after September 11. It widened surveillance and information-sharing authorities, expanded anti-money-laundering rules, and broadened terrorism offenses and immigration exclusions.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/107/public/56)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="patriot-2001"> I have read this</label>
:::

::: {.reading-card .domain-intelligence data-statute="fisa-amendments-2008"}
[FISA Amendments Act (702)](../../statutes/fisa-amendments-2008.qmd) [2008]{.reading-year} [Lapsed]{.status .status-lapsed} [Specific authorization]{.layer-badge}

Added Title VII to FISA. Section 702 lets the government target non-U.S. persons reasonably believed to be abroad, with compelled help from U.S. communications providers, under annual court-approved certifications instead of individual warrants.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/110/public/261), [current code](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/50/1881a?link-type=html)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="fisa-amendments-2008"> I have read this</label>
:::

::: {.reading-card .domain-intelligence data-statute="usa-freedom-2015"}
[USA FREEDOM Act](../../statutes/usa-freedom-2015.qmd) [2015]{.reading-year} [Partly expired]{.status .status-partly-expired} [Specific authorization]{.layer-badge}

The legislative response to the 2013 Snowden disclosures. It ended bulk collection of domestic telephone records and required that records requests be tied to a specific selection term.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/114/public/23)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="usa-freedom-2015"> I have read this</label>
:::

::: {.reading-card .domain-intelligence data-statute="risaa-2024"}
[RISAA](../../statutes/risaa-2024.qmd) [2024]{.reading-year} [Lapsed]{.status .status-lapsed} [Specific authorization]{.layer-badge}

Reauthorized Section 702 for two years, the shortest extension to date, and made the most extensive changes to FISA since 2008, concentrated on how the FBI may search collected data for information about Americans.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/118/public/49)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="risaa-2024"> I have read this</label>
:::

## Further reading

- [Cyber Info Sharing Act](../../statutes/cisa-2015.qmd){.subj}: Enacted as Division N of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2016. It set up a voluntary system for companies and the federal government to share cyber threat indicators and defensive measures, with legal protection for companies that take part.
- [Homeland Security Act](../../statutes/hsa-2002.qmd){.subj}: Created the Department of Homeland Security by merging 22 agencies, the largest federal reorganization since 1947.
- [National Security Act](../../statutes/nsa-1947.qmd){.subj}: The founding charter of the modern national security system. It created the National Security Council and the Central Intelligence Agency, established a separate Air Force, and placed the military departments under a single Secretary of Defense.

## Key terms

**Section 702**
:   The FISA authority, added in 2008, to target non-U.S. persons reasonably believed to be abroad with compelled help from U.S. providers, under annual court-approved certifications instead of individual orders.

**U.S. person query**
:   A search of lawfully collected data using a term associated with an American. RISAA's changes concentrated on how the FBI may run them.

**Sunset**
:   A date on which an authority expires unless Congress extends it.

## Check yourself

Try to answer each question before opening it.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon="false"}
## 1. What must the government show the FISA court for a traditional surveillance order?

That the target is a foreign power or an agent of a foreign power. See [FISA](../../statutes/fisa-1978.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon="false"}
## 2. What did the USA FREEDOM Act end?

Bulk collection of domestic telephone records; requests had to be tied to a specific selection term. See [USA FREEDOM Act](../../statutes/usa-freedom-2015.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon="false"}
## 3. How long did RISAA extend Section 702, and what did it focus on?

Two years, the shortest extension to date, with changes concentrated on how the FBI searches collected data for information about Americans. See [RISAA](../../statutes/risaa-2024.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon="false"}
## 4. What is Section 702's status in this wiki, and what should you check?

The wiki records it as lapsed after June 2026 with no reauthorization found. Check current status before relying on it. See [FISA Amendments Act (702)](../../statutes/fisa-amendments-2008.qmd).
:::
